source: PR #308 c923a2f; all live 143 IDs held
scope: Exact repairs discovered during independent academic review

sourceQuestionCorrections.issue: The UI collects four pairing decisions while answer.totalMarks is 8.
sourceQuestionCorrections.method: One independently correct complete nutrient→reagent+positive-result pairing earns one mark. Or create eight separately scored choices (reagent and observation) and re-QA each new stem.

sourceQuestionCorrections.issue: Colour comparison has no matched amounts, reagent volume or heating time; higher brick-red intensity need not indicate higher concentration without controlled conditions.
sourceQuestionCorrections.proposedPrompt: Two food extracts have the same sample volume and are tested with the same volume of fresh Benedict’s solution at the same hot-water-bath temperature for the same time. One tube turns green and the other forms a brick-red precipitate. Explain what this suggests about their reducing-sugar concentrations and one limitation of this test.
markPoints: The brick-red tube probably has a higher reducing-sugar concentration than the green tube under comparable conditions.
The colour scale gives only a rough comparison, not an exact concentration.

sourceQuestionCorrections.issue: No evidence is provided that positive/negative controls worked; do not interpret an unreliable negative experiment as proof of absence.
sourceQuestionCorrections.proposedPrompt: All four food tests on an unknown sample are negative. The positive and negative controls behaved correctly. Explain what can and cannot be concluded.
markPoints: None of starch, reducing sugar, protein or lipid were detected by these four tests under the conditions used.
This does not prove the sample contains no nutrients: the tests do not detect every nutrient and have detection limits.

sourceQuestionCorrections.issue: The source accepts 'starch is absent' as equally definite as 'not detected'. Prefer scientifically cautious interpretation.
sourceQuestionCorrections.proposedPreferredAnswer: No starch was detected by the iodine test.
reviewUnsafeOverclaim: The sample contains absolutely no starch under any conditions
A negative iodine test proves the sample is nutrient-free

sourceQuestionCorrections.issue: Starch negative should mean not detected, not proof of literal absence.
sourceQuestionCorrections.proposedScoringRule: Credit 'starch not detected' and correct equivalents; do not require absolute absence.

structuredCandidatePointRevisions.oldIssue: Three distractors use impossible changes of starch/air/graduation marks into glucose, so the answer is obvious.
structuredCandidatePointRevisions.stem: Which procedure could cause a false positive when a sugar-free food extract is tested with Benedict’s reagent?
structuredCandidatePointRevisions.correct: The same pipette transfers a drop of glucose solution left from an earlier sample
wrong: The sugar-free extract is measured into a clean test tube with a clean pipette
The food extract and Benedict’s reagent are heated for the same time as a negative control
The reagent volume is held constant while clean pipettes are used between samples

structuredCandidatePointRevisions.oldIssue: Closed-end colour visibility is a nonsensical distractor.
structuredCandidatePointRevisions.stem: Why must the open end of a hot Benedict’s test tube point away from people?
structuredCandidatePointRevisions.correct: Hot liquid can spit or splash out towards whoever the tube faces
wrong: It ensures the mixture stays at exactly the bath temperature
It prevents evaporation and therefore fixes the reagent concentration
It makes a positive colour change happen more quickly

structuredCandidatePointRevisions.oldIssue: Several distractors invent conversion between nutrients or claim larger means higher percentage.
structuredCandidatePointRevisions.stem: When comparing the iodine reactions of two types of bread, why use equal masses of bread?
structuredCandidatePointRevisions.correct: Unequal sample sizes could affect the amount of starch tested, making colour comparisons less fair
wrong: Equal mass guarantees both breads contain the same percentage of starch
Equal mass removes any need to control the volume of iodine reagent
